column3: The Hebrew actively says people reported to David; BSB uses passive “it was reported”.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The command explicitly says “arise, go down”; BSB compresses the actions to “Go at once”.
The fighting, driving off cattle, and striking are separate finite verbs; BSB makes the striking a participial clause.
The ephod is explicitly said to have come down in his hand; BSB makes Abiathar the subject bringing it with him.
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul again and calls the entrance fittings doors and a singular bar; BSB has a pronoun and “gates and bars”.
The Hebrew names “all the people” and explicitly says to go down; BSB has “all his troops” and omits the downward direction.
Close to the Hebrew.
The hearing verb is emphatically repeated; BSB has a single “has heard”.
The Hebrew answer repeats “he will come down”; BSB says only “He will”.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the dwelling verb and leaves David as a pronoun in the final clause; BSB names David there.
The life being sought is literally his “soul”; BSB renders this as taking his life.
Jonathan first arises and then goes; BSB gives only his coming.
Saul’s hand will not “find” David; BSB renders this as never laying a hand on him.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “come down” and says “the hand of the king”; BSB uses the second-person “your hand”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The location is expressed as where his foot will be; BSB replaces the foot image with where he goes.
The divisions of Judah are called “thousands”; BSB says “clans”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The wilderness of Maon is explicitly named twice; BSB uses “there” for the second mention.
“The mountain” is explicitly repeated for both sides; BSB states it only once.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew actively says people called that place; BSB has passive “is called”.
Close to the Hebrew.
